title: Where Did the Pond Birds Go?
locale: 山口県公立高校入試型
sentences: Our nature club wanted to know whether more wild birds were visiting a small pond behind the school.
A report from last year said forty birds were seen, but our first morning count found only twenty-eight near the water.
Ken worried that the pond was becoming less suitable for birds and proposed asking the town to plant more trees.
Mika looked at the old report carefully and found that last year's count had lasted two hours on a sunny afternoon.
Our own count had lasted just thirty minutes and had taken place before school on a cold and cloudy morning.
The different times made Ken stop and think, because a short morning count could miss birds arriving later in the day.
We asked our teacher how to make a fairer comparison, and she suggested choosing the same observation length and recording the weather each time.
For the next three visits, we counted for one hour at the same part of the pond while keeping a respectful distance from the birds.
On the first visit we counted thirty-one birds, on the second we saw thirty-seven, and on the third we recorded twenty-nine.
The second visit was sunny, while the other two were cloudy, so weather might have affected what we could see.
During our third visit, a loud machine started nearby, and several birds flew into the trees before we could record their positions.
I suggested writing down that noise rather than treating every difference as evidence of a long-term change in the pond.
We also looked at the photographs from last year and noticed that some birds had been counted twice after flying between two groups.
Our teacher said that photographs could help checking, but a single picture did not show every bird hidden among the reeds.
We created a simple rule: count birds in marked areas at fixed times, and record movements between areas separately.
The rule could not solve every problem, but it gave our club a clearer way to compare future visits with one another.
At our presentation, we showed all four recent counts, along with the time, weather, and unusual noise rather than one number alone.
Ken explained that the number twenty-eight was not enough to prove that the bird population had fallen.
We suggested continuing the counts across several seasons and sharing concerns about the environment only when better evidence supported them.
The town officer thanked us for caring about the pond while also admitting what our records could not show.
I learned that protecting wildlife starts with careful observation and honest questions, not with conclusions drawn from one quick count.
fullTranslation:
私たちの自然観察部は学校裏の池を訪れる野鳥が増えているのか調べようとしました。
昨年は四十羽と報告されましたが、今年最初の朝は水辺で二十八羽しか見つかりませんでした。
ケンは池が鳥にとって住みにくくなったのではと心配し、町に植樹を提案しました。
ミカは古い報告をよく読み、昨年は晴れた午後に二時間観察していたと気づきました。
今回の調査は寒い曇りの朝、登校前の三十分だけでした。
ケンは時間帯の違いに気づき、短い朝の観察では遅く来る鳥を見逃すかもしれないと考えました。
先生は観察時間を統一し、毎回天候も記録するよう提案しました。
その後三回、私たちは鳥に近づきすぎず、池の同じ場所で一時間ずつ観察しました。
一回目は三十一羽、二回目は三十七羽、三回目は二十九羽を記録しました。
二回目だけ晴れで、ほかは曇りだったため、天気も観察数に影響した可能性がありました。
三回目には近くで大きな機械が動き、数羽が位置を記録する前に木へ飛んでいきました。
私は数の違いをすべて長期的な変化の証拠とせず、その騒音も記録するよう提案しました。
昨年の写真を見ると、群れの間を移動した鳥が重複して数えられていた可能性もありました。
先生は写真は確認に役立つものの、葦に隠れたすべての鳥までは写らないと説明しました。
私たちは区域を決めた時刻に数え、区域間を移動する鳥は別に記録する規則を作りました。
この規則で全問題が解決するわけではありませんが、今後の比較はしやすくなります。
発表では新しい四回の観察数に、時刻、天気、騒音の情報も添えました。
ケンは、二十八羽という一回の数字だけでは鳥の個体数減少を証明できないと話しました。
私たちは季節をまたいで観察を続け、より確かな根拠を得てから環境への懸念を伝えることにしました。
町の職員は池を大切にする気持ちと、記録の限界を認める姿勢の両方を評価しました。
私は野生生物を守るには、短い調査で結論を急ぐより、注意深く観察し正直に疑問を持つことが大切だと学びました。

materials.title: Bird counts near the pond
materials.note: Counts may be affected by weather, observation length, bird movement and visibility.

questions.prompt: How long did the class's first count last?
questions.evidence: Our own count had lasted just thirty minutes and had taken place before school on a cold and cloudy morning.
questions.evidenceJp: 今回の調査は寒い曇りの朝、登校前の三十分だけでした。
questions.reason: 今回最初の観察は三十分。

questions.prompt: Which one-hour follow-up had the largest count?
questions.evidence: On the first visit we counted thirty-one birds, on the second we saw thirty-seven, and on the third we recorded twenty-nine.
questions.evidenceJp: 一回目は三十一羽、二回目は三十七羽、三回目は二十九羽を記録しました。
questions.reason: 三回の一時間調査で37羽が最大。

questions.prompt: Why did Ken reconsider his concern about the pond?
questions.answer: The counts had different times and durations.
questions.evidence: The different times made Ken stop and think, because a short morning count could miss birds arriving later in the day.
questions.evidenceJp: ケンは時間帯の違いに気づき、短い朝の観察では遅く来る鳥を見逃すかもしれないと考えました。
questions.reason: 去年と今年で観察条件が異なるため。

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement: A all follow-ups were sunny; B follow-up 2 was sunny; C the oldest count was thirty minutes; D the third follow-up had thirty-seven birds.
questions.evidence: The second visit was sunny, while the other two were cloudy, so weather might have affected what we could see.
questions.evidenceJp: 二回目だけ晴れで、ほかは曇りだったため、天気も観察数に影響した可能性がありました。

questions.prompt: Why might the third follow-up undercount birds?
questions.answer: A noisy machine made several birds fly into trees.
questions.evidence: I suggested writing down that noise rather than treating every difference as evidence of a long-term change in the pond.
questions.evidenceJp: 私は数の違いをすべて長期的な変化の証拠とせず、その騒音も記録するよう提案しました。
questions.reason: 騒音が鳥の観察機会に影響した可能性がある。

questionSetB.prompt: How much longer was last year's count than the class's first new count?
